what_its_for: Isradipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It belongs to a group of medicines called calcium channel blockers, which work by relaxing the blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take isradipine exactly as your doctor tells you. You may take it with or without food. If you are taking the controlled-release tablet (DynaCirc CR), swallow it whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep your blood pressure steady. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 2.5 mg taken twice a day (for regular capsules) or once a day (for the controlled-release tablet). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose based on how well your blood pressure is controlled. The maximum dose is usually 20 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store isradipine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking isradipine, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine may cause dizziness, especially when you first start taking it. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: chest pain or tightness, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles (especially if it is new or gets worse), sudden weight gain, shortness of breath, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also contact your doctor if your blood pressure readings remain high while on this medicine.
when_it_works: Isradipine starts lowering your blood pressure within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. Keep taking it even if you feel well — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, and this medicine works best when taken consistently every day.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially dizziness and low blood pressure. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Liver or kidney disease: If you have liver or kidney problems, your doctor may need to adjust your dose, so make sure to share your full medical history.
